Hi Alicia / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Recap: You’re evaluating Redwood for chat/transactional inference (tokenized PII fields, payment metadata). Main legal/privacy asks were around data controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice timing, and data residency for EU customers.
- Action items we took: I attached our current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v2.pdf) and a short security & privacy FAQ.

Next steps:
1) Please send a prioritized list of questions or any redlines you want us to review (Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx is fine).
2) I’ll loop in our legal lead (Marissa) and privacy partner (Rachel) for formal responses and proposed language.
3) If you confirm required residency (EU-only) or retention policy (you mentioned ~13 months), we’ll scope options (regional tenancy vs. contractual residency).

Open questions I have for clarity:
- Will Acme be the controller for customer data and expect Redwood to operate as processor (typical for integrations)?
- Is the 13-month logging/retention requirement a firm compliance need or a max/default?
- Any specific subprocessors you’re already concerned about (e.g., analytics, monitoring, cloud infra)?

Please reply with the prioritized list and I’ll get Marissa and Rachel into the thread.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks Ben — appreciate the recap and the docs. Quick answers and our prioritized asks below.

1) Controller/Processor: Acme will be the controller for customer payment data. We need confirmation Redwood will act as processor and accept processor obligations (data processing terms).
2) Subprocessors: Please provide the current list of subprocessors and the notice process for additions. We have a strict policy that requires at least 30 days notice for new subprocessors and an objection mechanism.
3) Breach notice: Our security team requires notification within 72 hours of discovery and a brief remediation plan.
4) Data residency: For EU customers, we require data to be processed and stored within the EU; can Redwood support regional tenancy or contractual residency guarantees?
5) Retention & logging: We generally need audit logs retained for 13 months; is that configurable per-customer?

Attaching an initial spreadsheet of our questions so your legal team can respond inline (Acme_DPA_questions.xlsx).

Let us know timeline for legal to respond — we’re aiming to have DPA terms agreed before final procurement review next week.

Best,
Alicia

Ben / Rachel / Alicia — thanks for the clear list. High level legal position below; I can produce proposed contract language by EOD.

- Controller/Processor: Confirmed — Redwood will act as processor. We will sign processor-side obligations in the DPA; Acme remains controller. (Standard clause offered).
- Subprocessors: Redwood maintains a current subprocessor list in our portal and provides notice of additions. Our standard notice period is 30 days with an objection right; if an objection is raised we’ll work to provide mitigation or support a transition. I will include portal link and current list in the DPA exhibit.
- Breach notice: We commit to notifying customers without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of discovery for incidents affecting customer data. The DPA will include our incident response commitments and a requirement to provide a remediation plan and regular updates.
- Data residency / EU: We offer region-specific hosting for EU customers via Dedicated or Private deployments. For hosted accounts, we can provide contractual commitments for EU data residency for certain tiers — however, additional operational controls (dedicated tenancy or VPC) may be required. I will outline the options and pricing impact.
- Retention & logging: Audit log retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private customers; for hosted plans we have default retention (90 days) with options to extend via add-on for up to 13 months. I’ll include the configurable options and how they are implemented (contract + console settings).

Attachments: I’ll send a short legal position memo (Legal_Position_DPA.docx) and a redline of the DPA with suggested language. For now, Ben — please ask Acme if they can share one or two clauses they intend to redline first so we can prioritize.

Marissa Cole
